PullRequest.Title: Tab moves focus into the empty editor hint
PullRequest.Body:
In a new, empty file VS Code shows a hint such as "Generate code (Ctrl+I), or select a language (Ctrl+K M). Start typing to dismiss or don't show this again." Its links can only be clicked with the mouse: keyboard and screen reader users cannot reach them (#132085). The same applies to the experimental list of actions that `workbench.editor.experimental.emptyEditorHintActions` shows instead (#347850).

With this change, **Tab moves keyboard focus into the hint** while it is shown and the empty editor has focus. In an empty document Tab would otherwise only insert indentation.

- **Classic hint:** Tab focuses the first link. The links are focusable buttons (`tabIndex=0`, `role=button`) with the theme's focus outline. Enter or Space runs a link, Tab/Shift+Tab and the arrow keys move between links, and Escape or Shift+Tab on the first link returns focus to the editor.
- **List of actions:** Tab focuses the first row; the arrow keys already move between rows. Shift+Tab from a row returns focus to the editor; Escape still hides the list, as before.
- **Typing is not lost:** typing a character, a dead key or IME input while focus is in either hint moves focus back to the editor before the browser handles the key, so the character lands in the document and dismisses the hint as usual.
- **Screen readers:** the hint's announcement now says "Press Tab to focus the hint." The classic hint's announcement on editor focus had stopped working (its `isVisible` flag was never set since a 2023 refactoring), so it is announced again, still controlled by `accessibility.verbosity.emptyEditorHint`.

The Tab keybinding (`editor.action.focusEmptyEditorHint`) uses the context key `emptyEditorHintVisible`, set while either hint is shown, and requires `editorTextFocus` and `!editorTabMovesFocus`. Its weight is below other editor contributions, so accepting a suggestion, an inline completion or a snippet placeholder still wins. In tab focus mode (Ctrl+M) Tab already moves focus, and the browser reaches the now-focusable links in order. Shift+Tab in the editor is unchanged.

Fixes #132085

## Validation

- Unit tests in `emptyEditorHintActions.test.ts` cover focusing, moving between links, Enter, Escape, Shift+Tab and typing for both hints, and the context key.
- Keyboard-only in Code OSS with both settings: Tab into the hint, arrow keys, Shift+Tab and Escape back to the editor, Tab then typing `x` inserts `x`, Enter on "Generate code" starts inline chat. With tab focus mode on, Tab moves through the links natively.
- Workbench typecheck (tsgo) and oxlint on the changed files.

## Supersedes

This takes over the ideas of these community pull requests; thank you to their authors. It covers both hint variants, returns focus to the editor and keeps typed characters:

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or recreate a classic hint in an empty text editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing eager contribution determines eligibility and constructs the content widget before the hint renders. The diff adds one context key, a cached keybinding lookup, and one disposable keyboard listener per existing link; DOM construction remains memoized by getDomNode().

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean and forward the existing small 'shown' telemetry record to configured appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One record per widget creation, not per link or focus movement; telemetry opt-out, metered-connection gating and bounded initialization buffering still apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same widget constructor already emitted the same shown record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous record preparation; no new awaited delivery is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One widget per eligible editor, containing 2–4 fixed links. Existing eligibility and activated-agent checks can scale with decorations and agents, but their frequency is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous widget creation and listeners; no new task fan-out. Variant changes dispose the old widget before creating its replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getDomNode() retains the rendered node for the widget lifetime. The global keybinding resolver is lazy and cached until bindings change; existing hint command lookups already create it before the new focus-command lookup. No new cache keys grow with documents.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, memoized DOM creation, bounded link generation, keybinding resolver and disposeHint ownership were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling was performed; the number of simultaneously eligible empty editors varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is small and bounded; listeners and context reset are registered for disposal, and the contribution drops the widget reference.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, resize or refresh the experimental action-list hint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing row construction and layout must finish before display. layout() still performs its pre-existing width write and offsetHeight read. The new stored ActionBar reference and extra focus-command label lookup do not add layout calls or row rebuild events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the remembered alternate-editor identifier from profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-memory Map lookup per row rebuild; zero database reads per rebuild after storage initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every row rebuild already called getPrimaryEditor and read the same cached preference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous cached read only; database initialization is not newly requested or awaited here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing shown telemetry record when the list fits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One record per fitting widget creation; row refreshes and keyboard focus do not newly emit shown records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fitting-widget constructor emitted the same event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing telemetry preparation, without a new awaited boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 2–4 fixed action entries plus one separator per widget; existing agent/editor registry scans scale with those registries, not one boundary call per registered editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous row refresh and layout on the existing configuration/agent/editor events. The context-change listener filters for chat.enabled, so changes to the new visibility key do not trigger additional row rebuilds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Row refresh clears the DisposableStore and replaces the ActionBar; the new field retains only the current instance. The keybinding resolver is shared and cached. Alternate-editor storage reads use an initialized memory cache, including absent values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor subscriptions, fixed group generation, row replacement/disposal, context filtering, layout and storage cache implementation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry sizes and resize frequency are unmeasured; expensive pre-existing layout behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No additional registry fan-out, hidden heavyweight allocation, forced-layout cycle or retained ActionBar history is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Tab into the hint, navigate links or rows, and return to the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Keybinding resolution selects the new command, which synchronously focuses the first existing link or ActionBar item. Arrow navigation changes focus among existing controls. Escape/Shift+Tab focuses the editor. If the standard contribution cannot focus a hint, the fallback triggers the existing tab editor command.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active editor per gesture; classic indexOf searches at most four links. ActionBar focus(0) targets one existing row rather than rebuilding the list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal single-threaded browser keyboard dispatch; no promises, subprocesses, filesystem, database, network or IPC operations are added to navigation. DOM focus can incur normal browser focus work but does not invoke the existing action handlers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Navigation reuses the rendered DOM and current ActionBar and the cached keybinding resolver. No document/model load or external service read is initiated by the focus command.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command handler, classic keyboard handler, ActionBar focus/updateFocus, editor focus and notebook contribution fallback were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser focus costs depend on the workbench DOM, but the change does not establish repeated layout or collection-wide reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. The new synchronous work is the bounded work required for the requested focus transition.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type from a focused hint, dismiss it, or switch editor models
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new hint-node keydown handler classifies the key and focuses the editor for character/dead-key/composition input. Existing model-content updates then determine hint eligibility and dispose it. Model/variant replacement still follows the existing disposal path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One classification and at most one editor-focus call per qualifying hint keydown; the listeners belong to one widget, not all documents. No input text is copied or serialized by the helper.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser input and existing editor update events. The debounce listener and all newly added DOM listeners are registered in the widget DisposableStore.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No input cache or history is introduced. Widget DOM, link references, ActionBar and listeners are bounded by widget ownership; disposed widgets are removed from editor widget maps and the contribution clears its reference.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper, caller registration, content/model subscriptions, widget disposal and CodeEditorWidget removal were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: IME/browser event timing is not profiled; correctness of character delivery is outside this performance-only pass.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable memory or repeated-work regression. There is no new unbounded retention, duplicated model update loop or expensive boundary on the changed input path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Announce the classic hint when editor text regains focus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing editor-focus debounce waits 500 ms and verifies text focus, a nonempty label and the verbosity setting. Removing the permanently false visibility guard restores the intended status announcement; the announcement is not awaited before typing or focusing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace text in one of two shared ARIA status DOM nodes and toggle its visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded status insertion per qualifying debounced focus callback; two shared nodes are reused and message insertion is capped at 20,000 characters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unchanged isVisible field remained false, so the classic hint's focus callback never called status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the focus debounce, off the initial keyboard-focus critical path; no external I/O or synchronous geometry read is performed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one surviving callback per widget per 500 ms debounce window, gated by current text focus. The message is a fixed hint and keybinding label, not document content.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One debounced callback per widget; no queued announcement history or concurrent external calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The hint label is constructed once per classic widget. status reuses two shared containers rather than accumulating nodes, and the debounce subscription is disposed with the widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: removed guard, debounced subscription and concrete status DOM implementation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Screen-reader and browser announcement costs vary, but no scaling or blocking mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Restoring a bounded, delayed announcement is intentional behavior, not evidence of excessive rendering or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate a hint action with Enter or Space instead of clicking
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The classic keyboard handler calls the same link.click() handler once, and the action list uses its existing ActionBar execution. Only explicit activation invokes commands, language selection, editor reopening or configuration changes; focusing/navigation does not eagerly run them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate extensions interested in the selected command via extension-host proxies when required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one activation RPC per interested extension-host manager per cold activation event; manager promises coalesce repeated event requests and completed/uninteresting events avoid RPC. Not per action-list entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Mouse activation executed the same command with the same extension activation/cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing registered-command behavior may await cold activation once hosts are ready; warm execution bypasses it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: After a language is selected, optionally synchronize the resource to the language-detection worker and send one detection request when URI guessing does not suffice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one worker detection request for the selected resource; worker creation is lazy and reused. Auto-detect is not offered for the empty document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same language-picker command already performed this work after mouse selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing post-selection detection is fire-and-forget and does not delay the language change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the hidden-hint setting through the existing configuration editor and text-file save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update per explicit Don't Show Again activation; actual save occurs only when the edit changes content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Mouse activation initiated the identical setting update and save path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing update promise is not awaited by the hint handler; configuration writes are serialized through its existing Queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remember the successful alternate-editor ID and eventually persist pending storage changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One constant-key store attempt after a successful single-editor reopen; identical values return early and pending writes coalesce by key before a delayed flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same successful mouse-triggered reopen already remembered the editor ID with the same storage lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the existing reopen completes; persistence is deferred rather than newly awaited by the hint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare the same small action/command telemetry records for existing appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hint-action event per activation and the existing command event where applicable; no event is added per navigation key or list entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The corresponding mouse action emitted the same records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing record preparation; external appender delivery behavior is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing selected-editor resolution/replacement or inline-chat session creation, which can invoke feature-specific extension-backed initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected editor or one inline-chat session per explicit action, with unchanged downstream initialization. No list-wide parallel invocation is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Clicking the same hint action entered these same resolver/session paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The same action-specific promises and ordering remain; the diff only adds a keyboard route to them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected action and one editor per gesture. Reopen narrows tab selection to this editor before the existing grouped command, so its effective resource cardinality is one, not all selected tabs or registered editors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One action is dispatched per keyboard activation. Existing extension activation may parallelize over host managers, settings writes remain serialized, reopen narrows to one editor, and no new fan-out across links/rows/resources is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Extension activation uses cached per-event promises and resolved-event flags. Detection reuses its worker. Storage reads/writes retain existing cache and coalescing. Selected feature initialization remains on explicit activation rather than hint construction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for before/after equivalence: handlers, click dispatch, command activation caches, language action, single-editor reopen, configuration queue and storage coalescing were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Feature-specific extension initialization, remote host latency and telemetry transport differ by environment and were not executed; those costs and invocation counts are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression. Newly accessible activation reuses existing expensive paths without increasing their per-action cardinality or moving them onto focus, render or ordinary typing.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for PR #349454 (base 794308978b6d99a6268d7675f216867a78501e3f, head ebdf1a5ebed09b6887052576e5f6299daea84a41). Inspected the complete five-file inventory and every diff page, then traced focus handling, widget ownership, render invalidation, caches and action boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established. Static read-only review; no runtime durations were measured. Supporting guide was requested but the tool truncated its oversized output; learned-regression guidance was read.
